description_ru: Стадии сна от лёгкого до глубокого и фазы быстрого сна, зачем мозгу нужен отдых и как лучше засыпать. Научные факты простым языком.
text:
Most people spend about one third of their lives asleep. If you live to ninety, you sleep for thirty years. It sounds like a waste of time, but sleep is one of the most important things your body does. When you close your eyes at night, you are not really switching off. Your brain and your body are busy with a lot of hard work. Let us see what happens during a normal night.

When you fall asleep, you go through different stages. At first, you are in light sleep. Your heart beats more slowly, your body temperature drops a little and your muscles relax. You can still wake up very easily, and a small noise is enough. This stage lasts only a few minutes. Many people say that they are awake in this stage, but in fact they have already slept for a short time.

After that, you enter deep sleep. This is the most quiet part of the night. Your breathing is slow and regular, and it is very difficult to wake you. During deep sleep, the body repairs itself. It makes new cells, builds muscles and strengthens the immune system, which protects you from illness. Children and teenagers get more deep sleep than adults, and this is one reason why they grow so fast.

About ninety minutes after you fall asleep, something strange happens. Your eyes begin to move quickly under your eyelids, your breathing becomes irregular and your brain becomes almost as active as when you are awake. This stage is called REM sleep, from the English words "rapid eye movement". It is the time when you have your most vivid dreams. Your body, however, stays still, because the brain sends a signal to your muscles to stop them. This is lucky, because otherwise we would run around the bedroom every night.

During a night, you pass through these stages four or five times, and each full cycle takes about ninety minutes. In the first half of the night, you have more deep sleep. In the second half, you have more REM sleep. This is why you often remember the dream that you had just before you woke up. If someone wakes you in the middle of a deep stage, you feel confused and tired, which scientists call sleep inertia.

Why do we need all this? Scientists believe that sleep helps the brain to organise memories. During the day, you collect a huge amount of information, and your brain cannot keep everything. At night, it decides what is important, and it moves these things to a more permanent place. Students who sleep well after studying remember more than students who study all night. So the best way to prepare for an exam is to learn, and then to go to bed.

What happens when we do not sleep enough? After one bad night, most people are slower, more forgetful and more angry. After a week of short nights, the body suffers more seriously. A person feels hungry all the time, catches colds more often and finds it harder to concentrate. Doctors also say that years of poor sleep can increase the risk of heart problems. Even a short nap helps. A twenty-minute sleep in the afternoon can make you more careful and more cheerful. Sleep is not a luxury. It is as necessary as food and water.

How much sleep do you need? It depends on your age. A newborn baby sleeps about sixteen hours a day. Children between six and twelve need nine to eleven hours. Most adults need seven to nine hours, although some people feel fine with a little less. Some animals sleep much more, such as bats and lions, and some, like giraffes, sleep for only a few hours.

If you want to sleep better, try a few simple habits. Go to bed at the same time every night. Keep your room dark, quiet and a little cool. Do not drink coffee in the evening, and put your phone away an hour before bed, because the bright screen tells the brain that it is still day. These small changes can make a big difference. Tonight, when you go to bed, you are going to give your body its most important job, and it will thank you in the morning.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Язык между зубами, как для θ, но с голосом; звук мягкий и звонкий, не «з» и не «д».
Долгий звук «и»: губы растянуты, язык высоко впереди; держите его дольше, чем русское «и».
Короткий открытый звук, близкий к ударному «а»; рот открыт средне, язык в центре.
